title: Random Forests — Ask a Crowd of Trees
key_insight: A random forest is that crowd. Each tree trains on a slightly different sample and considers a random selection of features.
body:
## Ask a Crowd of Trees

One tree makes a shaky decision from one path. Ask many different trees and let them vote, and one odd path matters less.

A random forest is that crowd. Each tree trains on a slightly different sample and considers a random selection of features.

The variation makes their mistakes less alike. Voting handles categories, while averaging handles numeric predictions.
common_mistakes: Assuming more trees repair biased or bad data.
Trusting split importance as unbiased evidence.
Ignoring prediction cost when serving a very large forest.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “Ask a Crowd of Trees” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Random forests are dependable tabular-data models with little tuning.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Ask a Crowd of Trees” story, explain Random Forests without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
